counterfactual_tokens_per_char.basis: 4 characters per token, a commonly cited rough heuristic for English text. This is a DISCLOSED APPROXIMATION used only to size a hypothetical flagship call from a REAL served answer's character length -- it never substitutes for a real provider-reported token count on the actual-cost side of a receipt. Any record using this path sets counterfactual_tokens_estimated=true so it is never confused with a measured count.

change_log.authorization: Founder-ordered, dispatch D-BP168-M0-212 ('YES GEMMA!! ... Check those' against a supplied Anthropic rate card).
change_log.what_changed: Added seven rate rows this table was missing: claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-5, claude-fable-5, claude-mythos-5, and claude-haiku-3-5 (retired-tier, kept for historical transcript lookups only). The gap mattered concretely: bishop_cost_gate_recorder.py (a Stop hook, separate instrument, NOT previously wired to this table at all -- it carried its own hardcoded flat PRICE_IN_PER_MTOK=3.00/PRICE_OUT_PER_MTOK=15.00 constants, reused from librarian-mcp/src/server.ts's equally-flat VENDOR_PRICING) was verified this dispatch to be mispricing every real turn: claude-sonnet-5 turns overstated 50% (billed at this table's already-correct $2/$10 rate, not the hook's $3/$15), claude-opus-5 turns UNDERSTATED 40% (correct rate $5/$25, hook used $3/$15), and claude-sonnet-4-6 turns were priced correctly only by coincidence (its true rate IS $3/$15, but the hook had no way of knowing that -- it would have applied the same $3/$15 to a Fable 5 turn too, understating that 70%, or the same $3/$15 to a Haiku turn, overstating that 3x, had those models ever run). This dispatch rewired bishop_cost_gate_recorder.py to read the CURRENTLY-EFFECTIVE row of THIS table per turn, per the model actually recorded in the transcript's `message.model` field, instead of any hardcoded constant -- see that file's own change history for the wiring. This table's existing claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5 rows (already correct, added 2026-08-03/2026-08-20 by D-BP160-M0-033 and never wrong) needed no correction; only the missing rows were added. Every new row's input_per_mtok_usd/output_per_mtok_usd/cache_write_5m/cache_write_1h/cache_read figures were independently re-verified via a fresh WebFetch of https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing at 2026-08-26T23:55Z (this dispatch's own fetch, distinct from and corroborating D-BP160-M0-028's 2026-08-20T17:35:47Z snapshot) and cross-checked against https://www.aipricing.guru/anthropic-pricing/, which agreed on every figure with zero disagreements found. Also independently RE-CONFIRMED, six days after D-BP160-M0-033 first caught it: claude-sonnet-5's $2/$10 standing rate is still permanent as of this fetch -- the provider page still states the scheduled 2026-09-01 reversion to $3/$15 'will not occur.' No existing row was altered; this is an additive change only.
corroboration: Live WebFetch of https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, 2026-08-26T23:55Z (this dispatch), Model pricing table: claude-fable-5 $10/$50, claude-mythos-5 $10/$50, claude-opus-5/4.8/4.7/4.6 all $5/$25, claude-sonnet-5 $2/$10 (with the same permanent-pricing note as D-BP160-M0-028's snapshot, verbatim: 'The $2/$10 per million input/output token pricing for Claude Sonnet 5... is now the standard price. The previously scheduled increase to $3/$15... on September 1, 2026 will not occur.'), claude-sonnet-4-6/4.5 $3/$15, claude-haiku-4-5 $1/$5, claude-haiku-3.5 $0.80/$4 (retired except Bedrock/Google Cloud). Cache multipliers confirmed identical to the existing rows' basis: 5m write 1.25x, 1h write 2x, cache read 0.1x of base input.

Cross-check WebFetch of https://www.aipricing.guru/anthropic-pricing/, 2026-08-26T23:55Z: same per-model input/output figures for every model in this change_log entry, and independently states 'No expiring introductory rates are documented... making current pricing permanent' for Sonnet 5 -- agrees with the primary source, no discrepancy to report.

D-BP160-M0-028_anthropic_rate_card_history.json (this estate's own prior append-only rate-card history, snapshot 2026-08-20T17:35:47Z-anthropic-v1) -- opus-4.7/4.6 and haiku-3.5 figures cross-checked against that file's `rates` array and found identical to this fetch's figures, six days apart, no drift observed.

Claude Opus 4.5 was not in either the BP160 snapshot or the Founder's BP168 supplied card by explicit ID, but the Founder's card states 'Opus 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5' as one flat $5/$25 group and the live fetch's own table lists claude-opus-4-5 at $5/$25 alongside the rest of the Opus family -- consistent, no separate verification needed beyond the same fetch.

change_log.what_changed: No new rate row added here -- gemma2:2b is LOCAL Ollama inference (confirmed via `ollama list` on this machine, ID 8ccf136fdd52, and directly benchmarked in LianaBanyanPlatform/BISHOP_DROPZONE/M0_LOCAL_INFERENCE_MEASUREMENT_BP160.md), so it is covered by the existing local-member-hardware row below (provider: local, $0/mtok, verified_on 2026-08-03, verified_by FounderDenken) exactly the way gemma4:12b, llama3.1:8b, and mistral:7b already are. The actual fix was in the ALLOWLIST that resolves a raw Ollama model id to this table's model_id: LianaBanyanPlatform/BISHOP_DROPZONE/D-BP159-009_price_table_map.json's model_id_price_map.known_local_models was missing a gemma2:2b entry, which is why a benchmark run correctly reported it as unpriced_unknown_model rather than silently guessing it was free. That allowlist now maps gemma2:2b -> local-member-hardware, reusing this table's existing row and the estate's existing local_inference_no_api_cost costCategory vocabulary (D-BP159-009_cost_axis.js) rather than inventing a second one. This change_log entry exists for audit-trail completeness on the real price table side, per this file's own discipline of recording what changed and why even when no rate figure moved.

change_log.what_changed: Corrected the claude-sonnet-5 successor row (previously effective_from 2026-09-01, $3.00/$15.00, PROVISIONAL). The scheduled 2026-09-01 increase to $3/$15 was CANCELLED by the provider; standing rate remains $2.00/$10.00 with no end date. The cancelled row is NOT deleted -- it is retained below with status CANCELLED, its effective window neutralized so it can never be selected as a currently-effective rate (see that row's own note for the mechanism), so a future reader can see a change was announced and then withdrawn. The claude-sonnet-5 intro row's effective_until was extended from 2026-08-31 to null to reflect that the intro rate is now the permanent standing rate. Cache-read and cache-write (5-minute and 1-hour TTL) rates were added to every anthropic-provider row that previously carried only input_per_mtok_usd/output_per_mtok_usd; this closes the gap named in D-BP160-M0-026 (measured cache-read ratio 25.38:1 with no cache rate on file).

rates.note: DO NOT USE THIS RATE. Retained for history only. effective_until was deliberately set to 2026-08-20 (before effective_from, 2026-09-01), making the [effective_from, effective_until] window empty/inverted by construction -- findCurrentRate()-style selectors that require effective_from <= atIso <= effective_until can therefore never match this row for any real atIso, so it cannot be silently picked up as 'currently effective' by any consumer of this table. The live standing rate is the claude-sonnet-5 row above (effective_from 2026-01-01, effective_until null, $2.00/$10.00). No cache_write/cache_read fields are recorded on this row: this rate never went live, so no provider-published cache multiplier for it was ever confirmed, and none is invented here.
